title: Simple roots and coroots give rational bases and integral spanning sets
statement: Let $V$ and $W$ be finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q$-vector spaces [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] with a perfect bilinear pairing $\langle-,-\rangle:V\times W\to\mathbf Q$. Let $I$ be finite and let $P$ be a reduced crystallographic root pairing indexed by $I$: injective maps $a:I\to V$ and $a^\vee:I\to W$ satisfy $\langle a_i,a_i^\vee\rangle=2$, and the reflections $v\mapsto v-\langle v,a_i^\vee\rangle a_i$ and $w\mapsto w-\langle a_i,w\rangle a_i^\vee$ permute the two families with the same permutation of $I$. Both families span their rational spaces; all pairings $\langle a_i,a_j^\vee\rangle$ are integers; reduced means that proportional roots differ only by sign. Let $J\subset I$ be such that $(a_j)_{j\in J}$ is linearly independent and every $a_i$ or its negative is a sum with nonnegative integer coefficients of the $a_j$. Then $(a_j)_{j\in J}$ is a rational basis of $V$, $(a_j^\vee)_{j\in J}$ is a rational basis of $W$, and $$\sum_{j\in J}\mathbf Z a_j=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbf Z a_i,\qquad \sum_{j\in J}\mathbf Z a_j^\vee=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbf Z a_i^\vee.$$ Moreover every coroot or its negative is a sum with nonnegative integer coefficients of the simple coroots.
